questions.question: Which framework is the right first pick for a workflow that must resume after a crash, accept a human approval mid-run, and fan out to three retrievers in parallel?
options: CrewAI
LangGraph
AutoGen
Agno
questions.explanation: LangGraph is the only one of the four with a first-class checkpointer, `interrupt_before`/`interrupt_after` for human approval, and `Send` for parallel fanout with reducer-based merging.

questions.question: Why does LLM-selected routing cost more tokens per turn than explicit routing?
options: It pre-fetches the next node's tool results in parallel purely to hedge against network latency spikes.
It duplicates the full tool list and system prompt for every single agent in the crew on each turn.
A planner LLM call picks the next step each turn, adding prompt and completion tokens for every decision.
It sends the whole conversation history to a separate verifier model before accepting the next step.
questions.explanation: CrewAI's hierarchical manager and AutoGen's GroupChatManager both spend an LLM call deciding who goes next. LangGraph and Agno only spend tokens where you explicitly write `llm.invoke`.

questions.question: Proposer-critic dialogue in code review naturally maps to which framework's core abstraction?
options: AutoGen's GroupChat / ConversableAgent pair for multi-agent dialogue
CrewAI's sequential Crew with roles, tasks, and a linear process
LangGraph's StateGraph with typed state and conditional edges
Agno's single Agent abstraction composed with tools and memory
questions.explanation: AutoGen's core abstraction is two or more agents speaking in turns until an exit condition -- the native shape for a proposer-critic or teacher-student dialogue.

questions.question: Which framework has built-in storage drivers (SQLite, Postgres, Redis, Mongo, DynamoDB) attached directly to the Agent class for session and memory persistence?
options: LangGraph, via its Postgres/Redis/SQLite checkpointer classes
Agno, via storage drivers attached directly to the Agent class
CrewAI, via the `context` field passed between sequential tasks
AutoGen, via chat history and user-defined context objects
questions.explanation: Agno attaches storage drivers (SQLite, Postgres, Mongo, Redis, DynamoDB) directly to an `Agent` via `storage=` -- conversation sessions and user memories persist automatically as a session store, not a full graph checkpointer.

questions.question: You have a two-call summarizer: fetch text, summarize. Which option is the right framework choice?
options: LangGraph StateGraph — always reach for a framework first, since reliability requires checkpointing.
CrewAI with researcher + summarizer roles — separate roles make a two-step pipeline easier to reason about.
Plain Python with the provider SDK — no framework is the fastest framework for tiny pipelines.
AutoGen GroupChat — let two agents argue about the best summary until they converge on one answer.
questions.explanation: Every framework is another dependency. If the task is two LLM calls and a tool, plain Python is cheaper than any framework's setup cost -- no framework is the fastest framework.
